# The settings file

`config.json` in the data folder holds the settings of one server. Every key may be left out; what is left out takes its default. A file that cannot be read as settings is reported when the server starts, and the defaults are used; a wrong entry in a list (`access`, `shortcuts`, `appearance.colors`) is reported and skipped, and the rest of the file still counts. Keys the server does not know are kept.

The page writes some keys from Settings, and leaves every other key of the file as it was; the rest are written by hand. `aubergine settings path` prints where the file is, and `aubergine settings list` every key with its value now.

## An editor that completes the keys

The server writes `config.schema.json` beside `config.json` each time it starts (only when it changed). Add this line to `config.json` and an editor that reads JSON Schema describes and completes each key:

```json
{ "$schema": "./config.schema.json" }
```

The same schema is `docs/config.schema.json` in the repository, and `aubergine settings schema` prints it.

## `font`

A terminal’s text.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `font.family` | The fonts of a terminal’s text, as a CSS font-family list: the first one found is used. | `"Menlo, Monaco, \"DejaVu Sans Mono\", Consolas, monospace"` | Settings |
| `font.size` | The size of a terminal’s text, in pixels. | `13` | Settings |

## `theme`

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `theme` | Light, dark, or whichever the system is set to (`system`), following it when that changes. One of `light`, `dark`, `system`. | `"system"` | Settings |

## `appearance`

How the page looks beyond light or dark: the color theme of each, a terminal’s theme and cursor, and colors set by hand.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appearance.light` | The color theme drawn when the page is light: a built-in one of that kind, or the ID of a theme file of that kind. One of `light`, `high-contrast-light`, `solarized-light`, `gruvbox-light`. | `"light"` | Settings |
| `appearance.dark` | The color theme drawn when the page is dark: a built-in one of that kind, or the ID of a theme file of that kind. One of `dark`, `high-contrast-dark`, `solarized-dark`, `gruvbox-dark`, `nord`, `dracula`. | `"dark"` | Settings |
| `appearance.cursor` | The shape of a terminal’s cursor. One of `block`, `bar`, `underline`. | `"block"` | Settings |
| `appearance.cursorBlink` | Whether a terminal’s cursor blinks. | `true` | Settings |
| `appearance.terminal` | The color theme of every terminal that has none of its own, of either kind, built-in or of a theme file. Null: the theme the page is drawn in. One of `light`, `high-contrast-light`, `solarized-light`, `gruvbox-light`, `dark`, `high-contrast-dark`, `solarized-dark`, `gruvbox-dark`, `nord`, `dracula`. | `null` | Settings |
| `appearance.byTag` | Color themes for terminals by tag, in order: a terminal that has no theme of its own is drawn in the theme of the first entry whose tag it has (whatever the capitals) and whose theme is there now. At most 20. A wrong entry is skipped and the rest still count. | no entries | Settings |
| `appearance.titleFormat` | What a terminal’s title says after its name, on the canvas and at the head of a terminal in a browser tab of its own: a template, text with placeholders such as {state} and {folder} (see docs/templates.md). One line, at most 200 characters. A placeholder that is not known is skipped; a template that is wrong as a whole is the default. | `"{state} {exit} {untold} {messages} {activity} {copy} {list} {typed-by} {desktop} {resume} {people-only} {links} {tags}"` | Settings |
| `appearance.rowFormat` | What a terminal’s row in the list says on its second line: a template, as `titleFormat` is (see docs/templates.md). Compact, a row has no second line and says its state alone. One line, at most 200 characters. | `"{state} {step} {standing} {time} {people-only} {typed-by} {tags}"` | Settings |
| `appearance.customCss` | Whether your own stylesheet, `custom.css` in the data folder, is linked on the page when there is one (docs/custom-css.md). Off: the page is drawn without it, as with `?plain` after its address. | `true` | Settings |
| `appearance.colors` | Colors set by hand over the theme that is drawn: `"<color>": "#rrggbb"` for every theme, or `"[<theme id>]": { … }` for one theme alone (built-in or of a theme file), which wins. Written by hand only. | no entries | by hand |

## `shell`

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shell` | The whole path of the shell new terminals start. Null: your own `$SHELL`. | `null` | by hand |

## `defaultFolder`

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defaultFolder` | The folder new terminals start in (`~` may begin it). Null: the home folder. | `null` | by hand |

## `away`

What changed while you were away.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `away.afterMinutes` | After this many minutes without the page being looked at, coming back shows what changed meanwhile. 0 switches that off. | `30` | by hand |

## `agents`

Agents Aubergine starts.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agents.logPrompts` | Keep the prompts given to agents in the terminal’s note log. Turn this off if prompts may hold secrets. | `true` | by hand |
| `agents.claudeCommand` | The command line that starts Claude Code. It may be a whole launcher, such as `mytool launch -- claude`; Aubergine’s own flags are added at the end, or where `{flags}` is. | `"claude"` | by hand |

## `api`

Limits on calls made with API tokens. They apply from the next start of the server.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api.rateLimitPerMinute` | How many calls one API token may make in a minute. | `600` | by hand |
| `api.maxBodyBytes` | The largest request body the server takes, in bytes. | `1048576` | by hand |
| `api.activityLogMaxBytes` | How large the activity log may grow before its older half is dropped, in bytes. | `5242880` | by hand |

## `workflows`

Limits on workflows, and when a run counts as quiet.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workflows.maxElements` | How many steps one workflow may have. | `50` | by hand |
| `workflows.maxElementChars` | How long the text of one step (or the text for every step) may be, in characters. | `20000` | by hand |
| `workflows.quietAfterSeconds` | A running run is marked quiet when its terminal has printed for this many seconds after the last report. | `300` | by hand |

## `library`

The library: how long and how much a fetch of a Git source may take. They apply from the next start of the server.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `library.fetchTimeoutSeconds` | The longest one Git command of a refresh may run, in seconds. | `60` | by hand |
| `library.maxFetchMegabytes` | The largest file Git may write while fetching, in megabytes: a source that needs more is refused. | `100` | by hand |

## `messages`

Messages between terminals: how many, how often, and when a thread waits for the owner. They apply from the next start of the server.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `messages.perSenderPerMinute` | How many messages one sender may send in a minute, to anyone. | `6` | by hand |
| `messages.perPairPerHour` | How many messages may pass between the same two in an hour, both ways together. | `30` | by hand |
| `messages.pauseAfter` | After this many messages between two that are not the owner, without the owner having looked, the thread pauses. | `6` | by hand |
| `messages.maxUnread` | How many unread messages a terminal may have waiting. One more is refused. | `20` | by hand |
| `messages.nudgeIntervalSeconds` | The fixed sentence that says a message is waiting is not typed into the same terminal again within this many seconds. | `120` | by hand |
| `messages.keepDays` | Read messages older than this many days are left out of what is listed. | `30` | by hand |
| `messages.logMaxBytes` | How large the file of messages may grow before its older part is set aside, in bytes. | `4194304` | by hand |

## `describe`

What a terminal says about itself.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `describe.remind` | Whether an agent that stops with its terminal not named, or with no summary, is told once to set them. | `true` | Settings |
| `describe.pullRequests` | Whether the pull request of a terminal’s branch is asked of the `gh` tool, where that is installed and signed in. | `true` | by hand |

## `desktop`

Opening a canvas terminal in your own terminal application.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `desktop.app` | Which application opens a terminal on the desktop: `terminal` or `iterm` (macOS), or `command` for a command line of your own. Null: the usual one for this system, `terminal` on macOS, and `command` elsewhere once one is written. | `null` | by hand |
| `desktop.command` | For `command`: the command line, with `{file}` where the script file goes. It is started without a shell. | `null` | by hand |
| `desktop.openNew` | New terminals made in the page also open on the desktop. | `false` | Settings |

## `schedules`

Schedules.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schedules.lateWithinHours` | A time that passed while the server was stopped or the computer asleep still runs, marked late, when it is at most this many hours old; older, it is missed. 0: never late. It applies from the next start of the server. | `6` | by hand |

## `terminal`

Terminal access for programs with an API token: what is people only from the start, the limits, and the audit of typed text.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `terminal.protectNewSessions` | New terminals are “people only” from the start. | `false` | by hand |
| `terminal.protectAgentSessions` | New terminals that start an agent are “people only” from the start: a token typing into an agent is the riskiest case. | `true` | by hand |
| `terminal.inputCallsPerMinute` | How many input calls one token may make to one terminal in a minute. | `60` | by hand |
| `terminal.inputCharsPerCall` | How many characters one input call may carry. | `4000` | by hand |
| `terminal.inputCharsPerMinute` | How many characters one token may type into one terminal in a minute. | `20000` | by hand |
| `terminal.maxWaitingRuns` | How many commands may be waited for at once, over all terminals. | `8` | by hand |
| `terminal.auditInput` | Keep the text that tokens type, itself, in `input.log` in the data folder. Off: only its length and a fingerprint are recorded. | `false` | by hand |

## `access`

Reaching this server from another device or page. Written by hand only; a wrong entry is reported and skipped.

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `access.addresses` | HTTPS origins this server also answers under, through something on this computer that carries HTTPS to it. Read when the server starts. | no entries | by hand |
| `access.pages` | Origins of the pages of another Aubergine that may show this server. Read when the server starts. | no entries | by hand |

## `shortcuts`

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shortcuts` | Keys: a command’s name to a chord (`"Ctrl+Meta+J"`), a list of chords, or null for no key. A wrong entry is reported and skipped. | no entries | by hand |

| Key | What it is | Default | Written |
